questions.question: Skill India is an initiative launched by the government in ________ to train over 40 crore Indians in different industry-related jobs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2015.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Skill India is an initiative launched by the Government of India in 2015 to provide training and skill development to over 40 crore Indians in different industry-related jobs.**
 
• The objective of Skill India is to create a workforce that is** skilled, certified, and employable, and to bridge the gap between the demand and supply of skilled manpower in various sectors of the economy.**
 
• Skill India is a part of the **National Skill Development Mission, which was launched in 2015 **with the aim of creating a skilled workforce of 500 million people by 2022.
 
• Skill India offers various training programs and courses in partnership with industry bodies, training institutes, and other stakeholders, and provides financial assistance to candidates through various schemes and programs.
 
• The other options, i.e., 2010, 2012, and 2017, are incorrect as Skill India was launched in 2015.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC)** is the **implementing agency** for Skill India, and various ministries, such as the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Ministry of Rural Development, Ministry of Labour and Employment, etc., are involved in the initiative.
 
• Skill India covers various sectors, including **agriculture, healthcare, construction, tourism and hospitality, retail, automotive, electronics, beauty and wellness, etc.**
 
• The government has set up various institutions and programs under Skill India, such as Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), Skill Loan Scheme, etc.
 
• Skill India aims to provide a platform for the youth of the country to acquire skills that are in demand globally and to make India the skill capital of the world.

questions.question: National income is defined as ________.?

options.text: At factor cost. N. N. P
At factor cost G. N. P.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**At factor cost. N. N. P**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• National Income can be thought of as the total amount of money generated from everything produced in a country.
 
• National income is also known as net national product at factor cost __is sum total of incomes of residents of a country in a given period of time including capital consumption or depreciation. All payments that are made to factors of production like land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship are at factor cost at which goods and services are produced.
 __
 
• National income = net national product at factor cost
 
 
 
• In numerical, **National Income = C + I + G + (X - M)**; Where,
 
 
• C = Total Consumption Expenditure
 
• I = Total Investment Expenditure
 
• G = Total Government Expenditure
 
• X - M = Export - Import
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

According to Simon Kuznets, National Income can be calculated by three methods.

__
 
• Product Method- 

 
 
• In this method, the net value of final goods and services produced in a country during a year is obtained, which is called the final product.
 
 
 
• Income Method-
 
 
• In this method, a total of net income earned by working people in different sectors and commercial enterprises is obtained. By this method, NI is obtained by adding receipts as total rent, total wages, total interest, and total profit.
 
 
 
• Consumption Method-
 
 
• It is also called the expenditure method.
 
• Income is either spent on consumption or saving. Hence, National Income is the addition of total consumption and total saving.
 
 

 
• The national income in India is calculated by the Central Statistical Organisation.
 
• The Central Statistics Office (CSO), an attached office of the ministry, coordinates the statistical activities in the country and evolves statistical standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• GNP(Gross National Product): GNP includes only those goods and services that are produced by the residents of India whether working in India or Abroad.

 
 
• GNP = Consumption + Gross Private Investment + Government Expenditure + Net Exports + Net Factor Income from Abroad.
 
 
 
• NNP (Net National Product) is the value of goods and services produced in an economy during a year after subtracting the depreciation value lost by capital goods each year. It is NNP at market price because the value of goods and services are taken at its actual market rate.

NNP = GNP – Depreciation of capital goods​

questions.question: As a result of Green Revolution, import of food crops was _________ in India.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Green Revolution in India led to an increase in domestic food production, reducing the need for imports.**
 
• Green Revolution was started in India in 1965-68.
 
• The green revolution is referred to as a period when Indian agriculture was converted into an industrial system due to the adoption of modern methods and technologies.
 
• Indian agriculture made a transition from old and manual methods and new, innovative and technological methods.
 
• It included the use of products like High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, tractors, irrigation facilities, pesticides, and fertilizers which were either not used or used on a very limited scale.
 
• The Indian Green Revolution was the brainchild of M.S. Swaminathan. 
 
• M.S. Swaminathan is known as the Father of the Green Revolution in India.
 
• This revolution led to an increase in food grain production especially in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Indian Green Revolution was a part of the larger and global Green Revolution started by Norman Borlaug.
 
• Norman Borlaug is called the Father of the Green Revolution in the world.
 
• Norman Borlaug was given the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 for his contribution to saving over 1 billion people worldwide from dying of starvation.

questions.question: Which disease is caused by iron deficiency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anemia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Anemia __is caused due to deficiency of Iron.
 
• Anemia, also spelled Anaemia, is usually characterized as a decrease in the total amount of red blood cells (RBCs) or hemoglobin in the blood which mainly contains Iron as a significant body mineral.
 
• It can also be defined as the blood's ability to carry oxygen to decrease.
 
• As anemia gradually progresses, the symptoms are often unclear and can include feeling tired, fatigue, shortness of breath, or poor exercise capacity.
 
• Anemia that develops rapidly also has greater symptoms, which can include confusion, feeling one passing out, losing consciousness, or thirst. Until a person is visibly pale anemia has to be significant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Thyroid**

 
 
• The thyroid gland produces hormones that regulate the body's metabolic rate-controlling heart, muscle, and digestive function, brain development, and bone maintenance. Controlling metabolism is the main function of the thyroid gland.
 
 
 
• **Hypocalcemia**
 
 
• A condition in which the blood has too little calcium.
 
• 
 
It can be caused by a lack of vitamin D. It can also signal a condition of the four small glands in the neck (the parathyroid glands), the kidneys or the pancreas

 
 
 
 
• **Kwashiorkor**
 
 
• Lack of protein in the diet causes Kwashiorkor. Protein is found in every cell of the human body.
 
• Protein is needed in the human body's diet to repair and regenerate cells.
 
• This is how a healthy human body regenerates cells on a regular basis.
 
• Protein is particularly necessary for growth in children and during pregnancy.
 
• When the body is deficient in protein, growth and regular bodily functions slow down, and kwashiorkor develops.
 
• Proteins are in charge of keeping the body's fluid balance.
 
• Inadequate protein causes fluid to migrate to parts of the body where it shouldn't be, accumulating in the tissues.
 
• Fluid retention, often known as edoema, is caused by a fluid imbalance across the walls of capillaries.

questions.question: Who among the following had termed the Right to Constitutional Remedy as a ‘soul of the constitution’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** B.R. Ambedkar.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **B.R. Ambedkar had termed the Right to Constitutional Remedy as the 'soul of the constitution' because it ensures that every citizen can approach the court if their fundamental rights are violated.**

 
 
• The Right to Constitutional Remedy is enshrined in **Article 32 of the Indian Constitution** and is considered to be one of the most important fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• Vallabhbhai Patel was one of the founding fathers of the Indian Constitution and played a key role in the integration of princely states into India, but he did not term the Right to Constitutional Remedy as the 'soul of the constitution.'
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India and played a crucial role in shaping India's foreign policy and economic development, but he did not term the Right to Constitutional Remedy as the 'soul of the constitution.'
 
• Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India and played an important role in the drafting of the Indian Constitution, but he did not term the Right to Constitutional Remedy as the 'soul of the constitution.'
 
• **Hence, "B.R. Ambedkar" is correct answer.**

questions.question: The Election Commission conducts elections for ______, State Legislature and the posts of President and Vice President.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Parliament of India is the supreme legislative body of the Republic of India.
 
• The parliament of India comprises the President and the two houses- the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Rajya Sabha is called the Council of States and the Lok Sabha is the House of People.
 
• The President has the power to summon and prorogue either House of Parliament or to dissolve Lok Sabha.

Thus, we can say that the Parliament of India consists of the President, the Rajya Sabha, and the Lok Sabha. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Deputy Speaker**

 
• Article 93 deals with the appointment of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker.

 
 
• The inaugural holder of the office of the Lok Sabha was M. A. Ayyangar.
 
• The term length of the deputy speaker of the Lok Sabha is five years during the term of the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Speaker**
 
 
• The Speaker is chosen by newly elected members of Lok Sabha.
 
• There are no specific requirements for becoming a speaker.
 
• The Speaker must only be a member of the House of Representatives, according to the constitution.
 
• An understanding of the country's Constitution and legislation, procedure, and conventions of Parliament is a vital asset for the speaker.
 
• A member belonging to the rulling party is elected.
 
• The Deputy speaker presides over the Lok sabha when the Speaker is absent from the sitting of the House 
 
• Shri G.V. Mavalankar was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha. 
 
• Shri Om Birla is the current Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Which Five Year Plan Focused on rapid industrialization of heavy & basic industries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2nd.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct answer is option 3, which is the 2nd Five Year Plan.**
 
• ** The 2nd Five Year Plan was initiated in 1956 and continued till 1961.**
 
• The primary objective of the plan was to **promote heavy and basic industries, such as steel, coal, power, and machine tools, to boost the country's industrial growth.**
 
• The plan aimed to achieve an annual growth rate of** 7% in industrial production.** It also focused on increasing agricultural production and improving the standard of living of the people.
 
• The plan's success was marred by several factors, such as poor implementation, inadequate infrastructure, and the Indo-China war, which disrupted the economy.
 
• The 2nd Five Year Plan laid the foundation for India's industrialization and set the tone for subsequent plans.
 
• It emphasized the importance of **self-reliance and the need to reduce dependence on foreign aid and technology.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** ****The 1st Five Year Plan** was launched in** 1951** and focused on agriculture, rural development, and community development. It aimed to achieve an annual growth rate of 2.1%, but it achieved a growth rate of 3.6%.
 
• **The 3rd Five Year Plan **was initiated in** 1961 and continued till 1966**.
 
 
• It aimed to achieve a growth rate of 5.6% in industrial production and focused on** reducing poverty and unemployment.**
 
 
 
• ** The 4th Five Year Plan** was launched in 1969 and continued** till 1974**.
 
 
• It aimed to achieve an annual growth rate of 5.7% and focused on achieving self-sufficiency in food production, promoting exports, and reducing regional imbalances.
 
 
 
• **The 5th Five Year Plan** was initiated in **1974 and continued till 1979.**
 
 
• **​** It aimed to achieve an annual growth rate of 5.5% and focused on reducing poverty, improving the standard of living, and promoting rural development.
